title: Treasury coupon announcement (January mid-quarter block: 3-Year new issue + 10-Year and 30-Year reopenings + 6/13/26-week bills) — the session that publishes the SOMA rollover add-on for the January 15 settlement
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes), its four FlateDecode content streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt independently from Tm coordinates by THIS event's own never-assessed research rather than inherited from either proposal. SIX page-3 rows carry the announcement date `Thursday, January 07, 2027`, read verbatim: `13-Week BILL` and `26-Week BILL` (auction Monday, January 11, settle Thursday, January 14), `6-Week BILL` (auction Tuesday, January 12, settle Thursday, January 14), `3-Year NOTE` with NO `R` (auction Monday, January 11, settle Friday, January 15), `10-Year NOTE / R` (auction Tuesday, January 12, settle Friday, January 15) and `30-Year BOND / R` (auction Wednesday, January 13, settle Friday, January 15), against the page legend `R --denotes reopening` / `T --denotes TIPS`. The ~11:00 a.m. ET announcement slot is standing convention inherited from the sibling coupon-announcement ledgers and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the announcement itself
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09), per EVENT-RESEARCH.md's rule for an id that existed only as proposals. Both proposals were read in full first — `proposals/treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-07.from-treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12.json` and `...from-treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13.json` — and both are CONFIRMED, not corrected: composition (six securities) and the Mon/Tue/Wed shape reproduce exactly from an independent extraction of the same PDF. The 10-Year proposal's SOMA arithmetic ($26.21B maturing, ~$8.6B added to the 10-Year leg, ~$47.6B total accepted) also reproduces — and this research supplies the derivation it asserted: the reported `SOMA Holdings Maturing on Issue Date` equals the par value of NON-BILL SOMA Treasury holdings maturing that day PLUS TIPS inflation compensation, validated against four settled 2026 blocks, and the block splits that amount STRICTLY PRO-RATA BY OFFERING AMOUNT (exact to <$1.5M on 34 of 34 non-zero blocks since 2022-12). WHAT THIS EVENT ACTUALLY DECIDES, stated so a later session does not over-read it: NOT the coupon sizes. Treasury's quarterly refunding statement fixes nominal coupon sizes for its whole quarter and the November-2026-to-January-2027 quarter is set at the 2026-11-04 refunding, already tracked as `treasury-refunding-2026-11-04`; this announcement PUBLISHES them 64 days later. Base rates from api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query pulled 2026-09-09, TIPS excluded: 3-Year new issue $58B (30 consecutive since 2024-04-09), 10-Year reopening $39B and 30-Year reopening $22B (21 consecutive each when the mid-quarter reopening months are pooled, since 2024-03-12/13). NOTE THE SECURITY-TERM LABEL: the January reopenings are the SECOND reopening of the November refunding security and print as `9-Year 10-Month` / `29-Year 10-Month`, NOT December's `9-Year 11-Month` / `29-Year 11-Month` — a query written against the December labels returns the wrong series, and on the 10-Month series the raw API rows are additionally contaminated by 10-Year TIPS reopenings unless `inflation_index_security` is filtered out. DISTINCT FROM THE ALREADY-TRACKED `treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-14`, which announces the NEXT block (20-Year reopening, 10-Year TIPS new issue, four bills, auctioning 01-19/20/21). Different sessions, different securities, neither a duplicate of the other. The BILL sizes are the genuinely open numbers, and the measured January base rate is that the ramp lands AFTER this announcement, not at it (1 of 2). Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
